claims.text: The starting (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits a robust magnetocaloric response.
The starting alloy exhibits a robust barocaloric response.
The starting alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and undergoes crack propagation under cyclic loading.
Partial substitution of Ni by Co will refine the alloy's microstructure.
Partial substitution of Ni by Co will increase solid-solution strengthening.
Arc melting followed by controlled annealing and water quenching will produce a fine, uniform microstructure in the Co-substituted alloy.
The intervention will produce a more homogeneous phase distribution.
The intervention will refine grain boundaries.
The intervention will stabilize magnetostructural features.
Co-for-Ni substitution will increase grain-boundary cohesion.
Increased solid-solution strengthening and grain-boundary cohesion will reduce crack initiation and propagation.
Maintaining the electronic balance and atomic arrangement will preserve the magnetostructural coupling responsible for the caloric response.
The modified alloy will have greater fracture toughness than the unchanged alloy.
The modified alloy will have greater load-bearing capability than the unchanged alloy.
The modified alloy will retain magnetocaloric and barocaloric performance similar to that of the unchanged alloy.
The improved integrity and retained caloric response will occur under magnetic and pressure fields similar to the current operating conditions and near the original transition temperature.
Co substitution will not detrimentally shift the alloy's operational temperature window.
